title: config.Load fail-open on case-variant duplicate keys, and non-deterministic YAML diagnostics
objective: Make config.Load fail closed on JSON object keys that the decoder resolves ambiguously (a key differing only in case from a known key silently overwrites the decoded field), and make its diagnostics deterministic for YAML input with non-string keys, so Load can never return a configuration that its own Validate rejects and identical input always yields an identical error message.
specReferences: spec line 143 (tests must be deterministic and reproducible)
acceptance: config.Load NEVER returns a non-nil *Config together with a nil error when that Config would fail config.Validate
a JSON configuration containing both schemaVersion and a case-variant of it (for example sChemAVErsion) is rejected with a non-nil error instead of loading with a silently overwritten value
the same guarantee holds for case-variant collisions on other known top-level keys, not only schemaVersion
identical input always produces an identical diagnostic message, including YAML documents with non-string object keys
every configuration that loads successfully today on unambiguous input still loads with identical results
./scripts/verify-candidate exits 0, and the config fuzz target added by FJ-040 (internal/config/fuzz_test.go) passes once FJ-040 resumes
nonGoals: no change to the public configuration schema or to any accepted input that is currently unambiguous
no configuration-file size or parse-complexity limit: the unbounded configuration-file read recorded after FJ-030 is a separate gap and is explicitly NOT fixed here
no change to behaviour outside internal/config
nextAction: reject decoder-ambiguous duplicate keys so Load fails closed, make the non-string-key diagnostic deterministic, and add a regression test for each
notes: Opened 2026-10-03 by PM from defects found by FJ-040's own config fuzz target (internal/config/fuzz_test.go, internal/config/load.go). Discovered by the FJ-040 coder and cleaner stages; both reproductions were then confirmed independently by the PM. Neither is fixed inside FJ-040 because internal/config is outside FJ-040 allowedFiles, which cover only the four new test files.

F1 reproduction, 37 bytes: config.Load([]byte('{"schemaVersion":1,"sChemAVErsion":0}')) returns cfg with a nil error and cfg.SchemaVersion == 0, and config.Validate(cfg) then reports 'schemaVersion must equal 1'. The same holds for SCHEMAVERSION. PM-confirmed independently. Mechanism: encoding/json matches object keys to struct fields case-insensitively, so the second key overwrites the decoded Config.SchemaVersion, while validateDocument inspects the raw document by exact key (root["schemaVersion"] == 1) and validateValues never re-checks cfg.SchemaVersion. rejectDuplicateJSON in load.go catches exact duplicate keys only, so a case-variant pair passes it. Effect reachable from untrusted input: a document violating the schemaVersion contract loads with a nil error, and readers such as the control API /meta configSchemaVersion observe 0. This is a fail-open violation of the project rule that strict behaviour must fail closed, and it is the same class as unknown keys, which spec 12.3 says MUST fail validation.

F2 reproduction, 6 bytes: 300 calls of config.Load([]byte('{07,2}')) produced 175 and 50 of two different diagnostics across runs (PM measurement: 250x 'convert YAML configuration: object key 7 is not a string' and 50x '... object key 2 is not a string'). Mechanism: normalizeYAMLValue ranges over a map[any]any and reports the first non-string key it encounters, and Go map iteration order is randomised. Spec line 143 makes determinism a project principle, so a diagnostic that varies between identical calls is a defect; the FJ-040 fuzz target detected it via an assertion that identical calls yield identical diagnostics.

FJ-040 is parked at status blocked with blocker type dependency trackedBy FJ-064. FJ-040's coder produced candidate 525ee08845fbb909 (four new test files, chain specifier in=out=8c80ab29, coder in=8c80ab29 out=525ee08845fb, cleaner in=out=525ee08845fb) and its cleaner made no change. FJ-040 cannot land green until this item is fixed, because its config fuzz target asserts exactly these two properties, so guard fuzz would exit non-zero and ./scripts/verify-candidate would fail.

Choosing a fix: the PM deliberately does not prescribe the mechanism. Two candidate approaches are a case-insensitive collision check in the duplicate scan (since encoding/json resolves keys case-insensitively, any case-insensitive collision is a genuine ambiguity) or a post-decode consistency check that the decoded value matches the raw document. The specifier and coder should choose, justify, and cover OTHER known top-level keys rather than special-casing schemaVersion, because the same silent-overwrite mechanism applies to mode, server, limits and the rest.

Deliberately out of scope and NOT to be folded in: the unbounded configuration-file read recorded after FJ-030, and yaml.v3 anchor/alias parse-cost amplification measured by the FJ-040 cleaner (a 62,837-byte alias-using document allocating about 51.7 MB in 97 ms). If bounding those turns out to be necessary for the FJ-040 fuzz target to be reliable, that is a separate decision and a separate ticket.
